title: Before you generate: give your creator agent a better starting point
description: Reduce repeated work with a resource-first agent workflow: discover existing tools, verify access, test a small sample and preserve editable project source.
sections: The most useful first prompt is often a request to inspect the project. Before an agent generates a soundtrack, builds a game system or invents a publishing pipeline, ask it to find existing skills, tools, examples and prior results. Ootle Lobby separates discovery, learning and agent skills so each can answer a different part of that search.
Available is not the same as connected

A resource appearing in a catalog does not prove that a tool is installed, an account is authenticated or a model is accessible. Ask the agent to distinguish those states. An engine workflow may require an editor installation; a hosted model may need a token; a stock-media workflow may need access to your licensed account. Keep credentials out of prompts that will be committed or shared.

For a trailer, audition a short voice passage before rendering the whole film. For a game, test the central interaction before producing every level. For a workflow, run one representative item before importing a large collection. Decide what acceptable means in advance: clear speech, correct output, playable behavior or a reproducible setup. A file existing is not the same as the experience working.
Save the recipe with the result

Keep the editable source, chosen settings, relevant dependencies and verification notes with the project. Preserve credits and access requirements without storing private tokens. When an approach fails, record the specific failure and the change that fixed it. The next agent should be able to continue from evidence instead of repeating the same costly experiment.

Give the next person a working starting point, a clear limit and a concrete next step. Skills are instructions, not proof that an integration is deployed. A local prototype, a tested export and a live service are different milestones. Naming the actual milestone helps creators choose what to reuse and what still needs testing.
author: Ootle Lobby
